source.title: Why Safeguarded Ships Run Aground? Aligned Large Language Models' Safety Mechanisms Tend to Be Anchored in The Template Region
source.authors: Chak Tou Leong; Qingyu Yin; Jian Wang; Wenjie Li

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether jailbreak attacks suppress a harmfulness signal defined by a difference-in-means probe, using probe measurements across template positions and layers rather than ablating or adding the original refusal direction. It also investigates related template-region mechanisms, but those results do not directly test the claim’s single-direction intervention.
record.gate_note: The study also reports region-level activation-patching results, TempPatch attack-success rates, probe accuracy, and probe transfer to generated responses. These bear on the topic but do not directly test a listed version, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. The detaching method’s attack results are not included as rows because they evaluate the study’s proposed method, not the claimed direction itself. Results cited from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study builds difference-in-means probes (harmful minus harmless residual streams, the Arditi recipe) at template positions. It measures whether successful jailbreaks lower the projection onto this direction, which bears on V3. Its detach method adds the same direction during generation and reports refusal recovering, which bears on V1's addition part. It never ablates the direction.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that aligned LLMs anchor initial safety decisions on information aggregated in the chat-template region (TASA). Successful jailbreaks suppress harmfulness features there. Steering response generation with template-derived harmfulness probes is a proof-of-concept that lowers ASR but does not remove the shortcut.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a difference-in-means linear probe, but its causal intervention patches template-region attention-head value states rather than projecting out or adding the direction throughout the residual stream.
record.method_sensitivity: The harmfulness probe varies across layers and template positions. The reported attack effect differs between successful and failed attacks; failed attacks show recovery of the harmfulness rate in middle layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Patching template-region value states from harmless inputs sharply increases ASR (TempPatch), and has a larger effect on the compliance probe than patching the instruction region, across 6 models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety decisions in aligned chat models rely mainly on information aggregated at chat-template positions.

fits_no_version.finding: Template-position harmfulness probes from middle layers classify harmful response content with high accuracy across response positions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A harmfulness direction derived from prompt activations transfers to generated tokens.

fits_no_version.finding: Residual-stream patching (Appendix B, Fig. 10) shows refusal-relevant states cluster in middle layers before the last template position. A trailing quote token acts as an extension of the template (Appendix E.2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-relevant signal is localized at specific template positions and middle layers.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The reported region-patching and attack-probe plots do not provide numerical values in the text. The probe's high cross-validation accuracy does not establish causal mediation. General capability preservation is not evaluated. The authors acknowledge that their mitigation is a proof-of-concept and does not eliminate the learned safety shortcuts.
record.rows_left_out: Section 5, Table 1 reports attack-success rates with and without the authors' proposed detaching method; omitted because these evaluate the study's new defense rather than the claimed direction. The text also reports attention-shift findings in Section 3.2, Figure 3 and Table 3, and a residual-stream causal-tracing case study in Appendix E.2, Figure 12; omitted because they do not test a listed claim version.

untested.parts: Directional ablation removing refusal and capability preservation; addition is tested only conditionally during generation, in 2 models.
Training against the direction's ablation for robustness; probing under the AIM attack; models other than Llama-3-8B-Instruct.
Not tested; per-layer and per-position probes are used but not compared to a single direction.
Not tested (only transfer from template to response positions).

missing.what: ASR with vs without adding the difference-in-means direction during generation (detach method). Gemma-2-9b-it: AIM 89.3→0%, AmpleGCG 62.3→5.7%, PAIR 94.3→11.9%. Llama-3-8B-Instruct: AmpleGCG 29.6→3.1%, PAIR 56.6→16.2%. These bear on V1's addition part.

record.verdict_notes: The study calls the direction a harmfulness/compliance probe, but it is computed exactly as Arditi's refusal direction (difference-in-means at post-instruction positions), so the V3 linkage is reasonable. The V3 evidence is observational: projection reduction in a single model, figure-only. No ablation shows the suppression is causal for the attacks' success.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not ablate or add the difference-in-means direction across layers and positions, or test whether such an intervention preserves general capability.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
The study measures whether attacks alter a difference-in-means harmfulness probe, but does not train models against ablation of the direction.
The study does not compare one direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account.
The study probes harmfulness features and safety decisions but does not test whether harmfulness judgment and refusal are separately encoded.
Probe transfer from template positions to response positions is reported, but transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models is not tested.
No refusal-training procedure or training-stage comparison is tested.

rows.subject: All models studied
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated a linear probe based on the difference between mean final-position residual streams for harmless and harmful examples using five-fold cross-validation.

rows.note: This establishes probe classification accuracy, not causal mediation by the direction.
rows.check: Probe validation accuracy (98.7±0.7%) is a method check, not a phenomenon result. It should probably not be a row.
